overview: The Seljuk Empire was a Turko-Persian Sunni state that conquered Iran, Iraq and Anatolia. It championed orthodox Islamic learning, built magnificent madrasas and mosques, and reshaped the political map of the medieval Middle East.

items.text: The Friday Mosque of Isfahan built and expanded, a masterpiece of Islamic architecture.
Persian miniature painting and calligraphy developed under Seljuk patronage.
Omar Khayyam composed his Rubaiyat and contributed to algebra and calendar reform.
The Nizamiyya madrasas established as a network of higher learning institutions across the empire.
The Battle of Manzikert opened Anatolia to Turkic settlement, transforming the region permanently.
Omar Khayyam's calendar reform produced a solar calendar more accurate than the Gregorian.
The Turkic settlement of Anatolia laid the foundations for the Ottoman Empire.
The madrasa system influenced Islamic education for centuries.

fall.text: The empire fragmented into smaller sultanates and was eventually conquered by the Khwarazmians.
